item.title: Russia Threatens UK Over Ukraine Using British Drones in Attacks
item.description: Russia warned the UK would face “consequences for which it will have to answer” after reports that Kyiv used drones made by British companies for strikes inside Russian territory.
item.dc:creator: Greg Sullivan

item.title: Trump Threatens Oman, Rejects Iran Truce Extension | Daybreak Europe 8/18/2026
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
The prospects for peace in the Middle East suffered a fresh setback, with President Donald Trump saying he’s not interested in extending the expiring agreement with Iran and tensions flaring anew in the Strait of Hormuz.
Meanwhile, sovereign borrowing costs surged around the world. Yields on 30-year US Treasuries rose to the highest since 2007 this week, while French borrowing costs hit the loftiest since 2008 and their German peers traded at 2011 levels.
Today's guest: Ellie Henderson, Investec, Economist. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan Agrees to Test Hypersonics, Other Missiles in Australia
item.description: Japan is set to test hypersonics and other missiles in Australia, underscoring the nations’ stepped-up defense cooperation.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Trump Cites India’s Elections to Push for US Voting Overhaul
item.description: US President Donald Trump cited India’s election system as a model for the US, bringing the world’s largest democracy into a contentious American debate over voter access and election security.
item.dc:creator: Swati Pandey

item.title: Australia Rolls Out Fresh Gambling Curbs After Divisive Debate
item.description: Australia’s government tightened proposed curbs on gambling advertising and marketing, though the restrictions fall short of demands from anti-betting lobby groups and some lawmakers.
item.dc:creator: Angus Whitley

item.title: Congo Ebola Outbreak: Financial Oversight Takes Priority as Distrust Grows
item.description: Ebola is reviving suspicions of profiteering in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where distrust over how response money is handled is undermining the community cooperation needed to contain the world’s fastest-growing outbreak.
item.dc:creator: Jason Gale

item.title: Myanmar’s Leader to Meet Putin on First Moscow Trip as President
item.description: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing is set to meet Russian leader Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, the former junta chief’s first trip to one of the isolated country’s closest allies since taking office in April after a widely criticized election.
item.dc:creator: Khine Lin Kyaw

item.title: South Korea’s Lee Pushes for Nuclear Sub Deal After Trump Rebuke
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called for swift progress in consultations with the US on the country’s plan to acquire its first nuclear-powered submarine after President Donald Trump ordered curbs on joint military drills with the ally, citing its lack of support for his war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: China’s Xi to Skip UN Meeting During Trip to US, Politico Says
item.description: Chinese leader Xi Jinping will forgo a stop in New York to address the UN General Assembly during a trip to the US next month to meet President Donald Trump, Politico reported.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Cockroach Janta Party: Why India’s Gen Z Movement Is a Challenge for Modi
item.description: What started out as a social media joke is turning into a serious headache for India’s political establishment, as the “Cockroach Janta Party” draws support from young people frustrated by a lack of jobs and a string of controversies surrounding the education system.
item.dc:creator: Aryan Gupta and Shruti Srivastava

item.title: Zambia’s Pro-Business President Wins Second Term in Election
item.description: Hakainde Hichilema was declared the winner of Zambia’s elections, an outcome that investors will welcome as he sets out to build on economic successes in Africa’s second-biggest copper producer.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hill and Taonga Mitimingi

item.title: Trump on Kim Jong Un: I Get Along With Him | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/17/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Republican Congressman Darrell Issa of California reacts to President Trump's threats against Oman, saying the President's comments should be taken "in context." Longtime Democratic strategist Jim Messina discusses Florida's primaries and whether democratic socialist candidates can broaden their appeal ahead of the midterms. Michael O'Hanlon, Director of Research in the Foreign Policy program at the Brookings Institution, assesses the Iran campaign so far, calling some of President Trump's decisions "impulsive." Former US Attorney General Alberto Gonzales says Attorney General Todd Blanche is "partly right" in arguing that the Justice Department should not operate independently of the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former AG: Blanche is 'Partly Right' on DOJ Independence
item.description: Former US Attorney General Alberto Gonzales says Attorney General Todd Blanche is "partly right" in arguing that the Justice Department should not operate independently of the White House, saying an attorney general should carry out a president's law-enforcement priorities but remain independent when it comes to investigations and prosecutions. Gonzales calls it "absolutely wrong" for a president to publicly direct an attorney general to investigate or prosecute someone without a legal basis. He also weighs in on the Justice Department's expanded election monitoring and efforts to obtain state voter rolls, saying "there is no evidence" of alleged massive voter fraud. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mexico’s Extortion Level Hits 11-Year High as Other Crimes Fall
item.description: Over 6,500 victims of extortion were reported in Mexico in the first six months of the year, the worst level in over a decade, according to a major business group.
item.dc:creator: Maya Averbuch

item.title: O'Hanlon: Trump's Iran Decisions Have Been 'Impulsive'
item.description: Michael O'Hanlon, Director of Research in the Foreign Policy program at the Brookings Institution, assesses the Iran campaign so far, calling some of President Trump's decisions "impulsive" while crediting him with showing restraint in avoiding attacks that could inflict mass civilian casualties. O'Hanlon says neither the US nor Iran has attractive options for escalation and expects the conflict to remain at a "low level of simmer" as both sides test the other's tolerance for economic pain. He says the US has the military means to overthrow Iran's regime if severely provoked, but doing so would require a ground invasion on the scale of Iraq and Afghanistan combined. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Messina on FL Primary, Dem 2028 Primary Calendar
item.description: Longtime Democratic strategist Jim Messina, who managed President Barack Obama's 2012 reelection campaign, discusses Florida's primaries and whether democratic socialist candidates can broaden their appeal ahead of the midterms. He also weighs in on the DNC's revamped 2028 presidential primary calendar, saying the new lineup could favor a candidate who can unite the party around cost-of-living issues. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Shouldn't Rush Iran Strategy: Rep. Issa
item.description: Republican Congressman Darrell Issa of California reacts to President Trump's threats against Oman, saying the President's comments should be taken "in context." Issa describes the confrontation with Iran as a 47-year problem and says Trump shouldn't feel pressured to resolve it on a political timeline, arguing that appearing to be in a hurry would play into Iran's hands. He also discusses conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln as the USS George Washington makes its way to the region to relieve the carrier. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Big Bend Border Project Paused After Bulldozers Arrive
item.description: The Trump administration is pausing work on a border security project inside Texas’ Big Bend National Park, days after bulldozers began clearing land in one of the least-crossed stretches of the US-Mexico border.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Trump Says North Korea’s Kim Jong Un Replied to Overtures
item.description: President Donald Trump said North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has responded to requests for the two leaders to have a conversation, as Trump moved to cut back military drills with South Korea, a longtime US ally.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian and Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: US-Iran Peace Prospects Dim as Trump Rejects Truce Extension
item.description: The prospects for peace in the Middle East suffered a fresh setback, with President Donald Trump saying he’s not interested in extending the expiring agreement with Iran and tensions flaring anew in the Strait of Hormuz.
